claim.quote: Here we demonstrate the production of antihydrogen atoms at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic environment.

key_value_text.quote: The neutral anti-atoms have been detected directly when they escape the trap and annihilate, producing a characteristic signature in an imaging particle detector.
key_value_text.value: Production of antihydrogen at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons

name: Production and detection of cold antihydrogen atoms

significance.quote: The neutral anti-atoms have been detected directly when they escape the trap and annihilate
significance.value: Direct detection of neutral antihydrogen annihilations by an imaging detector (no sigma level stated in the abstract)

summary.plain: ATHENA made antihydrogen atoms at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cold trap. It detected the neutral atoms directly when they escaped the trap and annihilated.
summary.technical: Production of antihydrogen at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic environment; the neutral anti-atoms are detected when they escape the trap and annihilate, producing a characteristic signature in an imaging particle detector.

title: Production and detection of cold antihydrogen atoms
why_it_matters: The abstract says that cold atoms and anti-atoms could form the basis of a new precise test of CPT invariance, which implies that they must have the same spectrum.
